scope: abstract auxiliary extensions of the retained I-P-N-Z-X chain through two auxiliary states, with exact Feshbach elimination and explicit J/grading/relation accounting

oneAuxiliary.forbiddenSupport: none when the attachment vector has support only on I,P
oneAuxiliary.failureOfDiagonalOnlyRequirement: both nonzero diagonals force the off-diagonal I--P correction lambda_I lambda_P/(z-M)

twoAuxiliaries.uniqueGenericDiagonalOnlyTopology: two disconnected massive leaves, one attached only to I and one only to P
twoAuxiliaries.genericConnectedTwoByTwoMassBlock: induces I--P through the off-diagonal auxiliary resolvent and therefore is not diagonal-only

jCompletedCost.oneSharedLeaf: one auxiliary state per sheet and its J partner: two new complex states, one mass and two attachment parameters before J conjugation
jCompletedCost.twoDisconnectedLeaves: two auxiliary states per sheet and two J partners: four new complex states, two masses and two attachment parameters before J conjugation

unconstrainedMassiveScalarAuxiliaries.gradingDecision: UNSAT as an ordinary grading-odd finite Dirac extension because each nonzero one-state mass M is a grading-even self term

strictGradingRelationAudit.oddAuxiliaryNormalForm: D_A=[[0,M],[M^*,0]] between opposite-chirality auxiliary subspaces on the same relation sheet
strictGradingRelationAudit.attachmentRule: a retained state couples only to auxiliary states of the opposite chirality
strictGradingRelationAudit.zeroEnergySelfEnergyTheorem: B D_A^(-1) B^* has zero diagonal blocks on each retained chirality, so every retained same-state self-energy vanishes at z=0 for any finite-dimensional invertible grading-odd auxiliary block
strictGradingRelationAudit.oneAuxiliaryState: cannot have an invertible grading-odd mass block
strictGradingRelationAudit.twoAuxiliaryStates: one opposite-chirality dimer is invertible, but its diagonal self-energies are proportional to z and vanish at zero; if attached to both I and P it also renormalizes I--P
strictGradingRelationAudit.twoMassiveDimersForSeparateRoles: requires four auxiliary states per sheet and four J partners, eight new complex states total; it gives diagonal-only lambda_r^2 z/(z^2-m_r^2) but no zero-energy mass
strictGradingRelationAudit.relationParity: the two members of each dimer must lie on the same relation sheet; J supplies the opposite sheet, where all edges and masses are conjugated
strictGradingRelationAudit.strictOneOrTwoAuxiliaryStateResult: UNSAT for nonzero zero-energy I and P diagonals
strictGradingRelationAudit.allSizeResult: UNSAT at zero energy for any invertible grading-odd auxiliary block unless grading or relation parity is relaxed

cofactorAndRank.effectiveMatrixAtZeroWithScalarLeaves: the five-chain with diagonal delta_I=-lambda_I^2/M_I and delta_P=-lambda_P^2/M_P
cofactorAndRank.reason: deleting P separates the I scalar block from the zero-diagonal three-chain N--Z--X, whose determinant is zero
cofactorAndRank.minimumForGapOnly: one grading-even massive leaf on I is sufficient if y h and its attachment/mass are nonzero; the P leaf is required only to generate both requested diagonals independently
cofactorAndRank.strictGradingAtZero: the induced diagonals vanish and the five-chain remains singular

intervalAndEFTDecision.supportStability: the two disconnected scalar leaves generate only I and P diagonals for every z away from their poles, so absence of I--N, P--Z and N--X is interval-stable
intervalAndEFTDecision.effectiveOperatorCofactor: cof_PP(D_eff(z))=0 identically for the same N--Z--X odd-chain reason
intervalAndEFTDecision.constantTextureStatus: only a low-energy EFT approximation for |z| much smaller than |M_r|
intervalAndEFTDecision.projectedResolventSelectedZero: not interval-stable: every finite projected diagonal resolvent has asymptotic 1/z and cannot vanish identically on an open interval
intervalAndEFTDecision.strictDimerExpansion: lambda_r^2 z/(z^2-m_r^2)=-lambda_r^2 z/m_r^2+O(z^3/m_r^4), a wavefunction-type correction with no constant mass

classificationDecision.oneSharedScalarLeaf: minimal if an induced allowed I--P correction and rank-one relation are accepted, but violates grading
classificationDecision.twoDisconnectedScalarLeaves: necessary and sufficient for independent diagonal-only I and P self-energies and exact forbidden-support stability, but violates grading
classificationDecision.strictOrdinaryFiniteGeometry: no one- or two-auxiliary-state solution, and in fact no finite grading-odd auxiliary block can generate nonzero zero-energy diagonals
classificationDecision.minimumReopeningDatum: either permit two grading-even massive correspondence leaves (four J-completed states) as EFT mediators, or explicitly relax the grading/relation rule; a strict finite-Dirac realization cannot obtain the desired diagonal masses by Schur elimination

physicalBoundary: This is a topology theorem for label-level auxiliary blocks. It does not source the leaves as Pati-Salam representations, derive their masses or couplings, or turn the energy-dependent effective kernel into a physical propagator without a lift and kinetic prescription.
